arxiv-2206-04199.title: Deep Surrogate Assisted Generation of Environments
arxiv-2206-04199.creator: Varun Bhatt, Bryon Tjanaka, Matthew C. Fontaine, Stefanos Nikolaidis
arxiv-2206-04199.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Varun Bhatt, Bryon Tjanaka, Matthew C. Fontaine, Stefanos Nikolaidis. Recent progress in reinforcement learning (RL) has started producing generally capable agents that can solve a distribution of complex environments. These agents are typically tested on fixed, human-authored environments. On the other hand, quality diversity (QD) optimization has been proven to be an effective component of environment generation algorithms, which can generate collections of high-quality environments that are diverse in the resulting agent behaviors.

arxiv-2307-02207.title: Spin-1 Thermal Targets for Dark Matter Searches at Beam Dump and Fixed Target Experiments
arxiv-2307-02207.creator: and Taylor R. Gray
arxiv-2307-02207.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by and Taylor R. Gray. The current framework for dark matter (DM) searches at beam dump and fixed target experiments primarily relies on four benchmark models, the so-called complex scalar, inelastic scalar, pseudo-Dirac and finally, Majorana DM models. While this approach has so far been successful in the interpretation of the available data, it a priori excludes the possibility that DM is made of spin-1 particles – a restriction which is neither theoretically nor experimentally justified.

arxiv-2401-01979.creator: Farmer Schlutzenberg
arxiv-2401-01979.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Farmer Schlutzenberg. We study some connections between definability in generalized descriptive set theory and large cardinals, particularly measurable cardinals and limits thereof, working in ZFC. We show that if κ \kappa is a limit of measurable cardinals then there is no Σ 1 ​ ( ℋ κ ∪ OR ) \Sigma_{1}(\mathcal{H}_{\kappa}\cup\mathrm{OR}) wellorder of a subset of 𝒫 ⁡ ( κ ) \mathcal{P}(\kappa) of length ≥ κ + \geq\kappa^{+} ; this answers a question of Lücke and Müller.

arxiv-2407-01898.title: Learning Granular Media Avalanche Behavior for Indirectly Manipulating Obstacles on a Granular Slope
arxiv-2407-01898.creator: Haodi Hu , Feifei Qian † , Daniel Seita † † Equal advising University of Southern California, United States haodihu@usc.edu
arxiv-2407-01898.description: Abstract Legged robot locomotion on sand slopes is challenging due to the complex dynamics of granular media and how the lack of solid surfaces can hinder locomotion. A promising strategy, inspired by ghost crabs and other organisms in nature, is to strategically interact with rocks, debris, and other obstacles to facilitate movement.

arxiv-2410-15734.title: A Kernelization-Based Approach to Nonparametric Binary Choice Models Thanks: Based on my job market paper, which was circulated as Nonparametric Estimation of Large Dimensional Binary Choice Models . I am grateful to my advisors Joon Y. Park, Yoosoon Chang, and Keli Xu for their advice. For helpful
arxiv-2410-15734.creator: Guo Yan
arxiv-2410-15734.description: Abstract We propose a new estimator for nonparametric binary choice models that does not impose a parametric structure on either the systematic function of covariates or the distribution of the error term. A key advantage of our approach is its computational scalability in the number of covariates.

arxiv-2411-09532.title: Quasi-centroids and Quasi-Derivations of low-dimensional Zinbiel algebras
arxiv-2411-09532.creator: Basdouri Imed 1 , Jean Lerbet 2 , Bouzid Mosbahi 3
arxiv-2411-09532.description: Abstract . In this paper, we introduce the concepts of quasi-centroid and quasi-derivation for Zinbiel algebras. Utilizing the classification results of Zinbiel algebras established previously, we describe the quasi-centroids and quasi-derivations of low-dimensional Zinbiel algebras. Additionally, we explore certain properties of quasi-centroids in the context of Zinbiel algebras and employ these properties to classify algebras with so-called small quasi-centroids.

arxiv-2506-20129.title: Taylor-mode automatic differentiation for constructing molecular rovibrational Hamiltonian operators
arxiv-2506-20129.creator: Andrey Yachmenev, Emil Vogt, Álvaro Fernández Corral, Yahya Saleh
arxiv-2506-20129.description: Abstract We present an automated framework for constructing Taylor series expansions of rovibrational kinetic and potential energy operators for arbitrary molecules, internal coordinate systems, and molecular frame embedding conditions. Expressing operators in a sum-of-products form allows for computationally efficient evaluations of matrix elements in product basis sets.

arxiv-2601-12568.title: One-loop c SW c_{\mathrm{SW}} for Wilson and Brillouin fermions with stout smearing or Wilson flow
arxiv-2601-12568.creator: Maximilian Ammer, Stephan Dürr
arxiv-2601-12568.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Maximilian Ammer, Stephan Dürr. We present results for the one-loop value of the improvement coefficient c SW c_{\mathrm{SW}} for Wilson and Brillouin fermions subject to stout smearing or Wilson flow, in combination with Wilson or Symanzik glue.

Metodología: Se realizó un estudio experimental in vitro con dos grupos: MTA convencional y

pmc-10599558.title: Evaluation of a novel lyophilized-pellet-based 2019-nCoV nucleic acid detection kit for the diagnosis of COVID-19
pmc-10599558.creator: Yiyuan Xu, Tian Xu, Shaoting Chen, Huakang Yao, Yuxiang Chen, Yanfen Zeng, Falin Chen, Guanbin Zhang
pmc-10599558.description: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has swept the world and poses a serious threat to human health. In the post-pandemic-era, we must remain vigilant against the co-infection of SARS-CoV-2 and other respiratory viruses. More accurate and convenient detection methods are required for the diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 due to its prolonged existence.

pmc-10745856.title: Two New Compounds from the Endophytic Fungi of Dryopteris crassirhizoma and Their Antimicrobial Activities
pmc-10745856.creator: Ping Hai, Yuan Gao, Lian Yang, Nie Chen, Haiyan Jia, Mengdie Wang, Huan Li, Wenli Jiang, Jian Yang, Rongtao Li, Rosanna Mallamaci, Filomena Conforti
pmc-10745856.description: Two endophytic fungi Trichoderma afroharzianum (HP-3) and Alternaria alstroemeriae (HP-7) were isolated and purified from the fresh root of Dryopteris crassirhizoma. Chemical investigation of the two fungi resulted in the isolation of two new phenols 2,4-dihydroxy-3-farnesyl-5-methoxy benzoic acid (1) and 2-hydroxyphenethyl 2-phenylacetate (2), together with 22 known compounds.

pmc-11655745.title: DNMT1 prolonged absence is a tunable cellular stress that triggers cell proliferation arrest to protect from major DNA methylation loss
pmc-11655745.creator: Salvatore Martino, Serena Gargano, Pietro Salvatore Carollo, Aldo Di Leonardo, Viviana Barra
pmc-11655745.description: Methylation of cytosine in CpG dinucleotides is an epigenetic modification carried out by DNA-methyltransferases (DNMTs) that contributes to chromatin condensation and structure and, thus, to gene transcription regulation and chromosome stability. DNMT1 maintains the DNA methylation pattern of the genome at each cell cycle by copying it to the newly synthesized DNA strand during the S-phase.

pmc-12428564.title: Heat Stress and Anthropogenic Substrates: Molecular and Behavioral Adaptation of Metridium senile in Human-Modified Marine Environments
pmc-12428564.creator: Guangliang Teng, Wen Chen, Xiujuan Shan, Qing Zhu, Xianshi Jin, Gad Degani, Makoto Kobayashi
pmc-12428564.description: Marine litter provides novel habitats for substrate-dependent species, potentially facilitating their expansion under climate change. This study investigated the thermal adaptability and substrate selectivity of the cold-water sea anemone Metridium senile in the Yellow Sea, where rising temperatures and anthropogenic substrates may drive its proliferation.

pmc-12513019.title: Gender differences in the impact of emotional support networks on health-related quality of life among floating elderly: a cross-sectional study in China
pmc-12513019.creator: Jinpeng Xu, Zheng Kang, Xiaoning Hao, Baojun Chen, Lingyu Zhao
pmc-12513019.description: BackgroundEmotional support, as a key component of social support, may influence the health of floating elderly individuals. This study aims to examine the characteristics of emotional support networks and assess their impact on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) among the floating elderly, with a focus on gender differences.

pmc-12589786.title: Isolated cardiac sarcoidosis: A systematic review
pmc-12589786.creator: Shokoufeh Hajsadeghi, Elham Piryaie, Shayan Mirshafiee
pmc-12589786.description: BackgroundIsolated cardiac sarcoidosis is a distinct entity of sarcoidosis characterized by disease confined exclusively to the heart, without involvement of other organs. While cardiac sarcoidosis can lead to severe complications such as arrhythmias and heart failure, isolated cardiac sarcoidosis remains understudied, and no systematic review has previously addressed this condition.

pmc-12613182.title: Impact of light pollution on the success of loggerhead turtle nesting in Chebba, Tunisia
pmc-12613182.creator: Imed Jribi
pmc-12613182.description: Background:Artificial light has a significant ecological influence and has become a worrying threat to some species, such as sea turtles, whose nesting and hatching may be impacted by light. The beaches of the Chebba area, following the Kuriat Islands, serve as one of the key nesting sites for Caretta caretta.

pmc-12695052.title: Susceptibility to Moral Arguments Among Liberals and Conservatives
pmc-12695052.creator: Fredrik Jansson, Pontus Strimling
pmc-12695052.description: An empirical result in Moral Foundations Theory is that liberals and progressives endorse the individualizing factors of care and fairness, while conservatives claim that the binding factors of authority, loyalty, and purity are equally relevant when determining what is moral. Does this translate into persuasiveness of arguments and opinion change?

pmc-12851249.title: Comparative study of heat-related symptoms among indoor and outdoor informal workers: A pilot study in Dhaka, Bangladesh
pmc-12851249.creator: Sheikh Mohiuddin Shahrujjaman, Bivuti Bhushan Sikder, Dilara Zahid, Syed Irfan Uddin
pmc-12851249.description: IntroductionRising temperatures and increasing extreme heat events pose severe health risks to informal workers, particularly those engaged in labor-intensive occupations. This pilot study investigates the comparative prevalence of heat-related symptoms among indoor and outdoor informal workers in Dhaka, Bangladesh, identifies key sociodemographic and occupational risk factors, and examines the association between heat stress and heat stroke.

pmc-12987300.title: Awareness, Understanding, and Use of Nutrition Labels on Pre-Packaged Foods and Their Associations with Noncommunicable Diseases Among Adults in Shanghai, China
pmc-12987300.creator: Wei Zhou, Jingyi Si, Yifan Gao, Weiwei Zheng, Ruifen Li, Changfeng Zhu, Xue Han, Jiajie Zang, Zhengyuan Wang
pmc-12987300.description: Background: Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) are a major global public health challenge and can be prevented and managed through a balanced, nutrient-rich diet. Food nutrition labels play an important role in guiding healthier choices, particularly for individuals at risk of chronic health conditions.

pmc-13147019.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2139 CHOROID PLEXUS ENLARGEMENT AFTER SPONTANEOUS SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE: LONGITUDINAL CHANGES AND ASSOCIATIONS WITH CLINICAL AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES
pmc-13147019.creator: Paula Roset, Inés Bartolomé, Daniel Santana, Alejandra Mosteiro, Ramon Torné, Mariano Werner, Carlos Laredo, Emma Muñoz-Moreno, Laura Llull, Sergio Amaro
pmc-13147019.description: Background and aimsThe choroid plexus (CP) is a key interface for cerebrospinal fluid regulation and neuroinflammatory signaling. However, its structural evolution and clinical relevance after spontaneous subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) remain poorly characterized.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 239 spontaneous SAH patients and 30 age and sex-matched controls was included.

pmc-13295596.title: Multi-Bioinformatics Approach Reveals COX5B-Mediated Modulation of Oxidative Phosphorylation and ROS Levels by Water and Ethanol Extracts of Schisandrae Fructus in SW1783 Cells
pmc-13295596.creator: Musun Park, No Soo Kim, Jin-Mu Yi, Seongwon Cha
pmc-13295596.description: Schisandrae Fructus is a traditional medicinal herb used to suppress hyperactivity and exhibits a wide range of therapeutic effects and few side effects; however, the molecular mechanism of action engaged by the multiple compounds found within Schisandrae Fructus remains insufficiently studied.

pmc-13454135.title: Hydrodynamic investigation of acoustic bubble–surface interactions on nanoarray-coated fins for microelectronic cooling with machine learning-based analysis
pmc-13454135.creator: Seyed Hamed Godasiaei, Pouyan Talebizadehsardari, Amir Keshmiri
pmc-13454135.description: This study presents a novel phase-change cooling strategy that synergistically integrates acoustofluidic bubble dynamics with nanoarray-coated micropin fins to enhance thermal performance. A multidisciplinary framework combines experimental measurements–heat transfer coefficient (HTC), heat flux, velocity fields, and pressure drop–across SS, S30–120, and S-nanosheet architectures with machine-learning models, including LASSO, Random Forest, and Deep Neural Networks.

pmc-13477543.title: Creating compassionate workplaces: A mixed-methods-based integrated framework on last aiders in the workplace
pmc-13477543.creator: Melanie Joshi, Julia Strupp, Helena Kukla, Golrokh Esmaili, Karin Ohler, Raymond Voltz, Georg Bollig
pmc-13477543.description: BackgroundSociety often perceives work and private life as separate spheres which leads to uncertainty about issues such as serious illness, dying, death, and grief within workplace settings. Last Aid Courses (LAC) are established to reduce uncertainty and insecurity towards these issues in the public, but not designed for use in the workplace.

pmc-13543572.title: Ligament of anterior horn of medial meniscus of knee joint: case reports and literature review
pmc-13543572.creator: Zhenyu Luo, Ke He, Yuan Li, Guanjun Sun, Yi Yin, Xu Peng

pmc-13546683.title: Association Between the Modified Furosemide Response Index and Prognosis in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on the MIMIC-IV Database
pmc-13546683.creator: Zhibin Chen, Guobao Hong, Hua Xiao, Qiaobin Wu, Kai Liu
pmc-13546683.description: BackgroundThe modified furosemide response index (mFRI), derived from a standardized furosemide stress test, is a biomarker of diuretic responsiveness and AKI progression. Its prognostic value in chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains unclear. This study examined the association between mFRI and clinical outcomes in critically ill patients with CKD.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the MIMIC‑IV database.

pmc-13609629.title: Structural Design of Ceramic Membranes to Mitigate Fouling in Membrane Bioreactors
pmc-13609629.creator: Boyang Yu, Chao Fan, Tuo Sun
pmc-13609629.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Despite the robust mechanical and chemical stability that make hollow flat-sheet ceramic membranes highly attractive for membrane bioreactors (MBRs), the fundamental relationship between their structural design, specifically pore size and structural symmetry, and biological fouling behavior remains elusive. To decouple the effects of membrane architecture on fouling mechanisms, a series of symmetric and asymmetric hollow flat-sheet alumina membranes were systematically engineered.
